meta.name: @archetype/design-system
meta.note: This file is the only place a value is typed. Everything in build/ is generated from it by scripts/build.mjs. DESIGN-SYSTEM.md carries prose rules and references tokens by name, never by value. If a hex appears in two places, one of them is wrong.

stone-50.name: Canvas
stone-50.use: Default page ground. The warm off-white that replaces #FFFFFF everywhere

stone-100.name: Chalk
stone-100.use: Secondary surface, sunken sections, raised cards on canvas

stone-200.name: Limestone
stone-200.use: Sunken ground, subtle hairlines, disabled control fill

stone-300.name: Ash
stone-300.use: Structural hairline, card frame, secondary action border

stone-400.name: Pumice
stone-400.use: Emphasis border, disabled text. NOT a type color at any size

stone-500.name: Stone
stone-500.use: Metadata on light grounds, rules, tertiary text at display sizes only

stone-600.name: Slate
stone-600.use: Reading copy, eyebrow, caption. The lightest tint that carries body text

stone-700.name: Graphite
stone-700.use: UI text, body-sm, emphasis. Holds serif hairlines at 15px

stone-800.name: Basalt
stone-800.use: Secondary dark ground, primary action hover

stone-900.name: Ink
stone-900.use: Display and heading type, primary action ground, dark page ground

verdigris-300.use: Accent on dark grounds, dark-mode link

verdigris-500.use: Muted accent, border and icon only. 4.38:1 on canvas — not body copy

verdigris-700.use: PRIMARY ACCENT. Links, active and selected states, focus ring

verdigris-900.use: Accent hover, text on cool tint, dark-mode cool surface

bronze-500.use: Warm hairline on dark. 3.00:1 on chalk — never type there

bronze-700.use: Warm accent. A hairline, a small mark, a single emphasized word

bronze-900.use: Text on warm tint, dark-mode warm surface

palette._note: The discipline, not an aspiration. Measured over painted area on any given surface.

semantic._note: Every value here is a color token name. A semantic entry that types its own hex fails the build. Reach for these in product code, never the raw ramp.

semanticDark._note: Overrides only. Any key here must also exist in `semantic`; the build fails otherwise. Applied under [data-theme="dark"]. Stone inverts; accents shift to their lighter steps because verdigris-700 on stone-900 is unreadable.

overlay._note: The only non-opaque colors in the system. Narrow use: a scrim behind a modal. No frosted glass, no backdrop-blur panels.

font._note: THE SWAP POINT. Three declarations, and every one of the 13 roles derives from them. Neue Haas ships as two separately-named optical cuts and both must stay independently addressable — that separation is what makes the 27/20 boundary enforceable. Two typefaces, three family strings.

proxy._note: Kept as the fallback path, not deleted. Archivo stands in for Neue Haas and Source Serif 4 for Freight Text Pro. Set `use` back to "proxy" to render the system anywhere the Adobe kit is not authorised — a fork, a sandbox, or a domain the web project does not cover.

kit._note: The Adobe Fonts web project carrying the production faces. It is domain-bound, so the package cannot bundle it — the consumer links this stylesheet and the stacks above pick the faces up. Consumers should read the URL from here rather than typing it, so it stays a single-source value like everything else.
kit.fontDisplayNote: Adobe serves the kit with font-display:auto, which blocks text while the faces load. It is a per-project setting in the Adobe Fonts web project UI and cannot be overridden from the URL — a ?display= parameter is ignored. Set it to "swap" there and update this field.

provides._note: Weights the kit actually ships, per family. The build checks that every weight the system uses is present, so dropping a weight from the Adobe project fails here rather than silently synthesising a face in the browser.

webfont._note: Proxy faces only, served from the Fontsource CDN. Production faces are loaded by the consumer's Adobe Fonts <link>, not here.

weight._note: Neue Haas numbering mapped to CSS. Two weights in normal use: 55 and 65. 75 is rare emphasis. There is no Light — never for body-adjacent text.

scale._note: One derived scale: 12 · 13 · 15 · 17 · 20 · 24 · 27 · 36 · 48 · 64. The display cluster 27/36/48/64 is an exact perfect fourth (1.333). 24→27 is 1.125, the text cluster's own interval, so the halves join on a real step. The text half is a gently widening progression (1.083 → 1.200), accepted rather than forced onto one ratio.

tracking._note: Negative on display, zero at body, slightly positive on UI and small caps. Never on lowercase text.
tracking.caption: 0.02em

role._note: The 13 roles. Each composes a `font:` shorthand from weight/size/leading/family, plus a matching tracking token. The shorthand cannot carry letter-spacing, so a consumer always sets both. `cut` is the optical size: display at 27px and above, text at 20px and below, nothing sans in between. `color` names the default semantic pairing.

measure._note: Long-form line length capped at 62–70 characters. Editorial publishing inheritance, and the reason the container is wide but the column is not.

space._note: 4px to 192px. The large steps exist so a generous gap reads as intentional confidence rather than an empty layout. Sections breathe at space-8 to space-9.

radius._note: Sharp by default. Corners are structural, not softened. `full` is reserved for the two places roundness carries meaning: status badges and the circular radio control. Rounding cards or buttons broadly is off-brand.

borderWidth._note: Hairlines do the structural work that photography or shadow does elsewhere.

shadow._note: Flat by default. Cards rest on a border, never a shadow. Shadows indicate elevation and are never decorative.

motion._note: Minimal and functional. Fades and color transitions only. No bounce, no spring, no parallax, no decorative motion.

logo._note: Geometry read from assets/logo/archetype-mark.svg, which is the only hand-authored logo file. mark-square, wordmark and lockup are generated from it by scripts/logo.mjs; the build fails if this block and the file disagree, or if a generated file is stale.
rules: The circle stroke is exactly half the triangle and crossbar weight — 10 against 20.
All three triangle points sit outside the circle. That is the current revision, not a drafting error.
The crossbar runs the full width and overhangs the circle by 0.34r each side. Never clip the bar to the circle — the overhang is the mark's distinguishing move.
Aspect is 1.24:1, not square. Set height and let width follow. Anything carrying 1.17:1 or 1.28:1 is stale.
Wordmark tracking is near-zero (0.02em), not wide. Wide tracking belongs to the eyebrow role, which echoes the wordmark rather than repeating it.

wordmark._note: Typesetting for the two files that carry live text. Declared, not derived — text advance width depends on the face and cannot be computed without rendering, so the canvas is a measured choice. letterSpacing IS derived: scale.tracking.wordmark x fontSize. Both files read it from here so they cannot disagree, which they did — the standalone wordmark shipped 1 against the lockup's 1.16, and 1.16 is the one the spec asks for.
wordmark.capHeightNote: Cap height as a fraction of font size, for Neue Haas Grotesk Display 75 Bold. Face-dependent: re-measure if the display family changes.

lockup._note: The stacked lockup: mark above, wordmark beneath. Both figures are fractions of the circle diameter, so the lockup rescales with the mark rather than with a fixed pixel gap.
lockup.bottomPadNote: All-caps has no descenders, so the baseline is the visual bottom. This is breathing room below it, in the mark's own coordinate space.

rules._note: Machine-checkable constraints. Each encodes a failure this system can actually have.

minContrast.why: eyebrow and caption at 12px — stone-500 measures 3.72:1 and fails
dark-mode secondary — stone-500 misses at 4.49:1, which is why this maps to 300
border and icon role only, explicitly not body copy

decorativeOnly._note: Never carries text on a LIGHT ground. stone-400 on canvas is 2.41:1 — it misses even the 3:1 large-text threshold, so it is not a display-type color either. It is legitimate text in dark mode, where it sits on stone-900, and legitimate as disabled state anywhere: disabled text is exempt from AA by design, and that exemption is the whole reason the token exists.

neverFill._note: Bronze prominent turns the brand corporate-luxury, which is the failure mode. It is a hairline, a small mark, or a single emphasized word.

barredValues._note: Values that must not appear anywhere in the generated output. Pure white breaks the warm cast the whole neutral ramp is built on.

warmCast._note: Every stone step must satisfy R > G > B. Neutralizing toward a cool or pure gray is the single change that would make the palette generic.

opticalBoundary._note: Display at 27 and above, text at 20 and below, nothing sans between. The only 24px role is quote, which is serif, so the gap is never tested. The build fails if a sans role lands in the gap.

readingSizes._note: Two reading sizes only: 17 and 15. There is no 19px step — body-lg was removed rather than adjusting the heading ramp.

retired.name: --color-charcoal-12
retired.reason: A tinted-transparent hover step that duplicated the overlay scrim at a different opacity. Two answers to the same question

retired.name: --color-navy-12
retired.reason: Navy was never in this palette. Carried over from a first pass that used a blue accent

retired.name: --color-ochre-12
retired.reason: Ochre was the working name for bronze before the ramp was built

retired.name: --color-border-default
retired.reason: "Default" said nothing about weight. The subtle/strong/emphasis triple does

retired.name: --text-body-lg
retired.reason: A 19px reading size. Removed rather than adjusting the heading ramp around it — two reading sizes is the rule

retired.name: --color-soft-white
retired.reason: Named for what it was not. The ramp names it Canvas

retired.name: --color-warm-sand
retired.reason: Folded into the stone ramp when the ramp was built

retired.name: --color-charcoal
retired.reason: Folded into the stone ramp. Charcoal was cool-cast, which broke the warm rule

assets._note: All logo files use currentColor, so set `color` on the parent to recolor. No fill attribute to override.

mark.use: Primary. Set height, let width follow

square.use: Favicons and app icons only — the mark centred on a square canvas

wordmark.use: Wordmark alone. Carries live text — see the outline note

lockup.use: Stacked mark over wordmark. Carries live text — see the outline note

liveText._note: The one exception to the single-point family swap. These two files hard-code a font-family attribute, so the build checks they still name the family the system is currently set to — the exception is unavoidable, drifting out of sync with it is not.

assets.outlineNote: archetype-wordmark.svg and archetype-lockup.svg carry live text with a font-family attribute, because an SVG loaded through cannot read CSS custom properties. They are the one exception to the single-point family swap and need editing alongside it. Supplying them as outlined vector removes the exception permanently and is the better fix — a wordmark should not depend on a webfont loading at all.

icon._note: Lucide, selected as the closest CDN-available match to the geometric-minimal aesthetic — thin, consistent stroke, no fill, no rounded joins. Flagged as a substitution: if Archetype commissions its own set, replace this. Icons are functional (chevron, close, check, arrow, link), never decorative, never a substitute for photography, and never emoji.
